method: ⚠️ THE METHOD CHANGED MID-SWEEP and every band below was RE-VERIFIED under the final one, so all four share one method.

FIRST ATTEMPT (abandoned): a per-band `grep -rIl` over the whole repo — one full-tree pass PER CANDIDATE. The measurement/ artifact tree is multi-GB, so this thrashed the SSD at ~170 MB/s per pass and was stopped by the owner. ⛔ Do not repeat it in a future round.
FINAL METHOD, ONE COMBINED PASS FOR EVERY CANDIDATE AND TRAP AT ONCE (regex `16[2-9]000000000`):
(a) TRACKED files  -> `git grep -lIE '16[2-9]000000000'` (reads PACKED OBJECTS, not the working tree; near-zero filesystem IO).
(b) UNTRACKED files -> exactly ONE filesystem pass, `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z | xargs -0 grep -lIE ...`.
(c) CLASSIFY per band by grepping only the (few) HIT FILES, never the tree again.

⭐ AND A BOUNDARY READING, which is the part that matters here: a band id is an INTEGER SEED, so a digit run that sits INSIDE A FLOAT MANTISSA can never be one. The classification pass reads one character either side of every hit.

incidental_digit_runs_recorded_so_the_ne.what: The abandoned full-tree pass reported 1-3 raw substring hits for EVERY id in 164e9..169e9 in this ONE file, and 34 for 170e9. Every one of them is a FLOAT MANTISSA TAIL — e.g. `"regret": 0.006164000000000003` contains `164000000000`.
incidental_digit_runs_recorded_so_the_ne.ruling: ⭐ NOT A BAND REFERENCE, AND THE READING IS NOT A JUDGEMENT CALL: a band id is an integer deck seed and these digit runs straddle a decimal point inside a float. A boundary-aware sweep — the id bounded by a non-digit and NOT preceded by `.` or a digit — returns ZERO for 164/165/166/167/168.
incidental_digit_runs_recorded_so_the_ne.⚠️: This is recorded because the parent round's rule was 'a band with ANY tree reference is not taken', and a naive substring sweep would refuse EVERY band in this range forever. The refusal rule stands; what is refined here is what counts as a reference.
